questions.question: Which of the following is known as the 'Steel City of India'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jamshedpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Jamshedpur is popularly known as the **Steel City of India** due to its massive steel production and industrial infrastructure.
 
• It was founded by **Jamsetji Tata**, the founder of Tata Group, in 1907 and serves as the headquarters of Tata Steel, one of India's largest steel manufacturers.
 
• The city is located in the state of **Jharkhand** and is one of the first planned industrial cities in India.
 
• Jamshedpur is renowned for its clean environment, well-maintained infrastructure, and contributions to India's industrial sector.
 
• It houses one of the largest steel plants in India, contributing significantly to India's economy and employment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Steel Industry in India:**

 
 
• India is one of the largest producers of steel globally, with major contributions from cities like Jamshedpur, Rourkela, and Bhilai.
 
• The steel industry plays a crucial role in sectors like construction, automotive, and infrastructure.
 
• India's steel production is driven by companies like Tata Steel, Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), and JSW Steel.
 
 
 
• **Tata Steel:**
 
 
• Tata Steel is one of the world's leading steel producers, headquartered in Jamshedpur.
 
• Founded in 1907, it operates one of India's first integrated steel plants and has a global footprint.
 
• The company emphasizes sustainability and innovation in steel production.
 
 
 
• **Planned Cities in India:**
 
 
• Jamshedpur is one of India's earliest planned cities, designed with a focus on industrial growth and urban development.
 
• Other notable planned cities include Chandigarh and Navi Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Jamsetji Tata:**
 
 
• Jamsetji Tata is often referred to as the "Father of Indian Industry" for his contributions to industrial growth in India.
 
• He envisioned Jamshedpur as a hub for steel production and a model industrial city.
 
• His legacy continues through the Tata Group's initiatives in various sectors.

questions.question: The Great Plains of India were primarily formed due to the deposition by which of the following rivers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus, Ganga and Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Plains of India are an extensive flat landmass stretching across northern India, formed primarily due to the deposition of sediments carried by the rivers **Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra**.
 
• These plains are also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plains and are one of the most fertile regions in the world due to rich alluvial soil deposited by the rivers.
 
• The sediment deposition process began millions of years ago when the Himalayas were formed, leading to erosion and transportation of materials downstream.
 
• The plains cover approximately 7 lakh square kilometers across northern and eastern India, including parts of Pakistan and Bangladesh.
 
• The rivers provided the necessary water and nutrients for agriculture, making the region a hub of ancient civilizations like the Indus Valley Civilization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• Alluvial soil is formed due to the deposition of sediments by rivers and is rich in minerals like potash, phosphoric acid, and lime.
 
• It is ideal for growing crops such as wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.
 
 
 
• **Indus River System:**
 
 
• The Indus River originates from Tibet and flows through India and Pakistan, contributing significantly to sediment deposition.
 
• It has several tributaries, including Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej.
 
 
 
• **Ganga River System:**
 
 
• The Ganga River originates from the Gangotri Glacier in the Himalayas and flows through northern India and Bangladesh.
 
• Major tributaries include Yamuna, Ghaghara, Gandak, and Kosi.
 
 
 
• **Brahmaputra River System:**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra River originates from Tibet and flows through northeastern India and Bangladesh.
 
• Its basin is one of the richest biodiversity hotspots in the world.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Great Plains:**
 
 
• The region supports a large population due to its fertile soil and abundant water resources.
 
• It plays a crucial role in India's agricultural economy, contributing significantly to food production.

questions.question: Which of the following is the largest Peninsular river?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godavari**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Godavari River is the **largest river in Peninsular India** and is often referred to as the "Dakshina Ganga" or the Ganges of the South.
 
• It originates from **Trimbakeshwar in the Nashik district of Maharashtra** and flows eastward across the Deccan Plateau.
 
• The river spans a total length of approximately **1,465 km**, making it the second-longest river in India after the Ganges.
 
• The Godavari basin covers an area of about **312,812 square kilometers**, encompassing states like Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, and Karnataka.
 
• Major tributaries of the Godavari include **Pranhita, Indravati, Sabari, and Manjira**, significantly contributing to its water volume.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Peninsular Rivers:**

 
 
• These rivers are non-Himalayan rivers originating from the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• Most of them are seasonal, relying heavily on monsoon rains for their flow.
 
• They generally have **short courses and flow eastward** into the Bay of Bengal, except for a few like Narmada and Tapi, which flow westward.
 
 
 
• **Narmada River:**
 
 
• It is one of the major west-flowing rivers in India and is often referred to as the "Life Line of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat."
 
• Originates from **Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh** and flows for about 1,312 km.
 
 
 
• **Mahanadi River:**
 
 
• It originates from **Sihawa in the Dhamtari district of Chhattisgarh** and flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The Mahanadi has a total length of approximately 858 km.
 
 
 
• **Kaveri River:**
 
 
• It originates from **Talakaveri in the Western Ghats in Karnataka**.
 
• The Kaveri River has a total length of about 800 km and is a major water source for Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

questions.question: The total length of the Northern Plain of India from west to east is approximately ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2400 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Northern Plain of India spans approximately **2400 km** in length from west to east, extending through the states of Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, and Assam.
 
• This vast plain is formed by the deposition of sediments brought by three major river systems: **the Indus, the Ganga, and the Brahmaputra**.
 
• It is one of the world's most fertile regions and forms a significant part of the **Indo-Gangetic-Brahmaputra Plain**.
 
• The plain is broadly divided into three sections: the Punjab Plains in the west, the Ganga Plains in the center, and the Brahmaputra Plains in the east.
 
• This region is characterized by alluvial soil, making it ideal for agriculture, and it supports a dense population.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Alluvial Soil:**

 
 
• Alluvial soil is the predominant soil type in the Northern Plain, deposited by rivers over thousands of years.
 
• It is rich in nutrients such as potash, phosphoric acid, and lime, making it highly fertile.
 
• The soil supports the cultivation of crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and cotton.
 
 
 
• **Rivers of the Northern Plain:**
 
 
• The Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra rivers, along with their tributaries, play a crucial role in shaping the plain.
 
• These rivers provide water for irrigation and contribute to the alluvial deposits.
 
 
 
• **Physiographic Divisions of the Northern Plain:**
 
 
• The Northern Plain is divided into the Bhabar, Terai, Bhangar, and Khadar regions based on their geological characteristics.
 
• Khadar (new alluvium) is the most fertile and is renewed annually by river floods.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• The Northern Plain is often referred to as the "Granary of India" due to its high agricultural output.
 
• It is also home to major cities like Delhi, Kolkata, and Lucknow, making it a hub for trade and commerce.

questions.question: Narcondam Island is located in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andaman Sea**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Narcondam Island** is a small volcanic island located in the **Andaman Sea**, part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands in India.
 
• The island is situated to the northeast of the main Andaman Islands and is a part of the Andaman district.
 
• Narcondam Island is an extinct volcanic island and is the second volcanic island in India after Barren Island.
 
• The island is known for its unique biodiversity and is home to the **Narcondam Hornbill**, a bird species endemic to the island.
 
• The Andaman Sea, where Narcondam Island is located, lies to the east of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands and is part of the northeastern Indian Ocean.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andaman Sea**

 
 
• The Andaman Sea is a marginal sea of the northeastern Indian Ocean bounded by the Andaman and Nicobar Islands to the west, Myanmar to the north, Thailand to the east, and the Malay Peninsula to the southeast.
 
• It is known for its rich biodiversity and is part of the Indo-Pacific region, which supports a variety of marine life.
 
• It is an important route for international maritime trade connecting the Indian Ocean with the Pacific via the Strait of Malacca.
 
 
 
• **Narcondam Hornbill**
 
 
• The Narcondam Hornbill (Rhyticeros narcondami) is a critically endangered bird species found only on Narcondam Island.
 
• It is listed as "Vulnerable" on the IUCN Red List due to its restricted habitat and threats from habitat loss.
 
• Conservation efforts are ongoing to protect this unique species and its habitat.
 
 
 
• **Barren Island**
 
 
• Barren Island, located near Narcondam Island, is the only active volcano in South Asia and is part of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• Unlike Narcondam, which is extinct, Barren Island has periodic eruptions, with the latest reported in 2017.
 
 
 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**
 
 
• The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are a group of islands located at the southeastern edge of the Bay of Bengal.
 
• They are a Union Territory of India and consist of 572 islands, of which 37 are inhabited.
 
• The islands are known for their strategic importance, rich biodiversity, and indigenous tribes such as the Jarawas and Sentineleses.

questions.question: The channel between Minicoy and the Maldives is known as the:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eight Degree Channel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Eight Degree Channel** separates the island of Minicoy (Lakshadweep) from the northernmost islands of the Maldives.
 
• This channel is named based on its approximate location along the **8°N latitude.**
 
• Minicoy is the southernmost island of the Lakshadweep group, located closer to the Maldives than to other Indian islands.
 
• The channel is strategically significant as it lies on important international shipping routes in the Indian Ocean.
 
• This waterway is used for maritime navigation and transportation between India and the Maldives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Minicoy Island**

 
 
• Minicoy is the second-largest island in Lakshadweep and is known for its cultural connection with the Maldives.
 
• The island features a lighthouse built in 1885, which serves as a navigational aid for ships.
 
• Minicoy has a unique linguistic and cultural heritage, with the locals speaking Mahl, a dialect of Dhivehi.
 
 
 
• **Geography of Lakshadweep**
 
 
• Located in the Arabian Sea, Lakshadweep is India's smallest Union Territory, comprising 36 islands.
 
• It is known for its coral atolls, reefs, and lagoons, making it ecologically and economically important.
 
 
 
• **Maldives**
 
 
• The Maldives is a nation of islands located in the Indian Ocean, southwest of India.
 
• It consists of 26 atolls and has a population predominantly dependent on fishing and tourism.
 
 
 
• **International Shipping Routes in the Indian Ocean**
 
 
• The Indian Ocean is a vital region for global maritime trade, connecting Asia, Africa, and Europe.
 
• Major shipping lanes pass through channels like the Eight Degree Channel, facilitating the movement of goods and energy resources.

questions.question: Which Indian State/Union Territory have the highest percentage of urban population according to the Census 2011?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the Census 2011, **Delhi** had the highest percentage of urban population in India, with **97.5%** of its population living in urban areas.
 
• Delhi is classified as a Union Territory with a unique urban-centric demographic profile due to its status as the national capital and a major metropolitan hub.
 
• Urbanization in Delhi is driven by factors such as migration, better economic opportunities, and the presence of a highly developed infrastructure.
 
• The total urban population of India as per Census 2011 was 377 million, which accounted for 31.16% of the total population.
 
• Delhi's urban population growth is significantly influenced by its role as a political, cultural, and administrative center of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urbanization in India:**

 
 
• Urbanization refers to the increasing proportion of a country's population living in urban areas.
 
• In India, urbanization is largely attributed to migration from rural areas in search of employment, better living standards, and access to education and healthcare facilities.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011:**
 
 
• The Census of India 2011 is the 15th National Census conducted by the Government of India, providing comprehensive demographic, social, and economic data.
 
• It classified the population into rural and urban categories based on specific criteria, such as population density, infrastructure, and employment patterns.
 
 
 
• **Factors Contributing to Urbanization:**
 
 
• Industrialization and economic development attract rural populations to urban centers.
 
• Availability of better infrastructure, healthcare, and education facilities in urban areas drives migration.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of Urbanization:**
 
 
• Rapid urbanization can lead to overcrowding, housing shortages, and strain on urban infrastructure.
 
• Environmental issues such as pollution and waste management become significant challenges in highly urbanized regions.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT located in the Andaman group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Minicoy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Minicoy** is part of the **Lakshadweep group of islands**, not the Andaman group.
 
• The **Andaman Islands** are located in the Bay of Bengal, while the **Lakshadweep Islands** are in the Arabian Sea.
 
• Minicoy is known for its distinctive culture and is the southernmost island of the Lakshadweep group.
 
• Other islands mentioned in the question—Havelock, Neil, and Barren—are part of the Andaman archipelago.
 
• The Andaman and Lakshadweep groups are geographically and administratively distinct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Andaman Islands:**

 
 
• Located in the Bay of Bengal, the Andaman Islands are part of the union territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• Famous islands include Havelock Island (now Swaraj Dweep) and Neil Island (now Shaheed Dweep).
 
• Home to the **Indigenous Andamanese tribes** and rich in biodiversity.
 
 
 
• **Lakshadweep Islands:**
 
 
• Located in the Arabian Sea, the Lakshadweep Islands are India's smallest union territory.
 
• Minicoy is the second-largest island in this group and culturally distinct due to its Maldivian influences.
 
• The islands are known for their coral atolls and lagoons.
 
 
 
• **Barren Island:**
 
 
• Barren Island, located in the Andaman group, is home to India's only active volcano.
 
• It lies approximately 135 km northeast of Port Blair.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Distinction:**
 
 
• The Andaman and Lakshadweep islands are separated by vast distances and are located in different seas.
 
• Andaman Islands are closer to Myanmar, whereas Lakshadweep Islands are closer to the Malabar Coast of India.

questions.question: What is the name of the point where India, China and Myanmar meet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Diphu Pass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Diphu Pass** is the tri-junction point where the boundaries of **India, China, and Myanmar** meet.
 
• It is located in the **easternmost region of Arunachal Pradesh**, India, in the **Patkai Hills**.
 
• The pass lies on the strategic **McMahon Line**, which serves as the boundary between India and China.
 
• Diphu Pass has historical significance, as it was a crucial route for trade and cultural exchanges between South Asia and Southeast Asia.
 
• It also plays a significant role in the geopolitics of the region, being part of the **India-China border dispute**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **McMahon Line**:

 
 
• It is the boundary line drawn between India and Tibet during the **1914 Simla Convention**.
 
• China disputes the validity of the McMahon Line, leading to ongoing tensions between India and China.
 
 
 
• **Patkai Hills**:
 
 
• The Patkai Hills are a mountain range located in the northeastern region of India, forming part of the border with Myanmar.
 
• They are known for their rich biodiversity and dense forests.
 
 
 
• **Tri-Junction Points**:
 
 
• These are points where the boundaries of three countries meet, often leading to strategic and geopolitical significance.
 
• Examples include the **India-Nepal-China tri-junction** and the **India-Bhutan-China tri-junction** at Doklam.
 
 
 
• **India-China Border Disputes**:
 
 
• Disputes primarily revolve around the regions of **Aksai Chin** (to the west) and **Arunachal Pradesh** (to the east).
 
• The border conflicts have led to several military standoffs, including the **1962 Sino-Indian War**.
 
 
 
• **Myanmar's Borders**:
 
 
• Myanmar shares a 1,643 km-long boundary with India, touching the states of **Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram**.
 
• The border is vital for trade and cultural connections between the two nations.

questions.question:
Which of the following states is landlocked and does not touch any international

boundary?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chhattisgarh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chhattisgarh** is a landlocked state in India and does not share its borders with any international boundary.
 
• It is surrounded by seven Indian states: Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The state was carved out of Madhya Pradesh on **November 1, 2000**, becoming the 26th state of India.
 
• Raipur is the capital of Chhattisgarh and serves as a major hub for administration and commerce.
 
• Chhattisgarh is known for its mineral wealth, being one of India’s richest states in terms of coal, iron ore, and other natural resources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Landlocked States:** A landlocked state refers to a region entirely surrounded by land without direct access to the sea or an international boundary.
 
• **International Boundaries of India:** India shares borders with seven countries: Pakistan, China, Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, and Afghanistan.
 
• **Geographical Features of Chhattisgarh:** The state has dense forests, rivers such as Mahanadi and Indravati, and a tropical climate, which contributes to its rich biodiversity.
 
• **Economic Significance:** Chhattisgarh is a leading producer of rice, and its forests contribute to India’s timber and minor forest produce economy.
 
• **Cultural Heritage:** The state is famous for its tribal communities and cultural landmarks, including the Bastar region and its traditional festivals like Bastar Dussehra.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Peninsular Plateau’s major divisions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Purvanchal Hills**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Peninsular Plateau is one of the oldest landforms in India, predominantly composed of igneous and metamorphic rocks.
 
• Its major divisions include the **Central Highlands** (north of the Narmada River) and the **Deccan Plateau** (south of the Narmada River).
 
• The **Northeastern Plateau**, though geographically distinct, is considered part of the Peninsular Plateau region as it is contiguous with the Deccan Plateau.
 
• The **Purvanchal Hills** are not part of the Peninsular Plateau; they are part of the Himalayan mountain system located in the northeastern region of India.
 
• The Purvanchal Hills include hill ranges such as the Patkai, Naga, Manipur, and Mizo Hills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Highlands:** Located to the north of the Narmada River, it includes regions like Malwa Plateau and Bundelkhand.
 
• **Deccan Plateau:** The largest plateau in India, it is bordered by the Western Ghats, Eastern Ghats, and the Satpura Range.
 
• **Northeastern Plateau:** Also referred to as the Meghalaya Plateau, it comprises Khasi, Jaintia, and Garo hills and is an extension of the Peninsular Plateau.
 
• **Purvanchal Hills:** A sub-mountain range of the Himalayas, these hills form the easternmost boundary of India.
 
• **Peninsular Plateau's Formation:** This plateau was formed due to volcanic activity and is part of the ancient Gondwana landmass.

questions.question: Where is Rohtang Pass located?

options.text: On the Shiwalik hills, near Dehradun
On the eastern Pir Panjal range, near Manali
On the Dhauladhar range, near Dharamshala
On the Zanskar range, near Kargil

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**On the eastern Pir Panjal range, near Manali**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rohtang Pass** is situated on the eastern Pir Panjal range in the Himalayas, near Manali in Himachal Pradesh, India.
 
• It is located at an altitude of approximately **3,978 meters (13,050 feet) above sea level**.
 
• The pass connects the Kullu Valley with the Lahaul and Spiti Valleys, playing a critical role in transportation and trade.
 
• The name "Rohtang" translates to "**pile of corpses**" in Tibetan, referencing the difficulties faced by travelers due to unpredictable weather conditions.
 
• Rohtang Pass is renowned for its scenic beauty and serves as a major tourist destination for adventure activities like skiing and trekking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pir Panjal Range:** It is a part of the Lesser Himalayas and stretches across Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir.
 
• **Atal Tunnel:** A strategically important tunnel under Rohtang Pass, inaugurated in October 2020, reduces travel time between Manali and Leh.
 
• **Climate:** Rohtang Pass experiences extreme weather conditions, with heavy snowfall during winters, making it inaccessible for several months.
 
• **Tourism:** The pass is a hub for adventure sports such as skiing, paragliding, and mountain biking, attracting thousands of visitors annually.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** The heavy influx of tourists and vehicles has raised concerns about environmental degradation in the region.

questions.question: The Eastern Peripheral Expressway is built to decongest traffic in _____.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Eastern Peripheral Expressway (EPE)** is a 135-kilometer-long expressway constructed to **decongest traffic in Delhi**, particularly by diverting non-essential traffic away from the city.
 
• It is part of the **Peripheral Expressway project** designed to create a bypass around Delhi, reducing the load on the city’s roads.
 
• The expressway connects major highways such as **NH-1, NH-2, NH-8, NH-24, NH-58, and NH-91**.
 
• The EPE is India's **first smart and green expressway**, equipped with **solar power plants, advanced traffic management systems, and rainwater harvesting systems**.
 
• It was inaugurated by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on May 27, 2018.
 
• The project aims to curb pollution in Delhi by reducing vehicular emissions caused by traffic congestion within the city.
 
• It also facilitates the smooth movement of goods and vehicles, improving connectivity between the states of **Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Delhi**.
 
• The expressway includes **several amenities such as rest areas, fueling stations, and surveillance systems** to ensure commuter safety and convenience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chennai**__

 __
 
• **Chennai** is the capital city of **Tamil Nadu** and is known for its **port-based economy**.
 
• It is a major hub for **automobile manufacturing** and is often referred to as the **Detroit of India**.
 
• The traffic issues in Chennai are addressed through projects such as the **Chennai Peripheral Ring Road (CPRR)** rather than the Eastern Peripheral Expressway.
 
 
 
• **Mumbai**__
 __
 
• **Mumbai**, the financial capital of India, is located in **Maharashtra** and faces significant traffic congestion.
 
• Projects like the **Mumbai Trans Harbour Link** and the **Western Express Highway** are designed for traffic management in Mumbai.
 
 
 
• **Bengaluru**__
 
 
• **Bengaluru**, the capital of **Karnataka**, is known as the **Silicon Valley of India**.
 
• The city’s traffic congestion is being addressed with projects like the **Bengaluru Peripheral Ring Road (PRR)** and the **NICE Road**.

questions.question: What type of vegetation is mostly found in the Thar Desert?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Low-growing plants and shrubs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Thar Desert**, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is primarily characterized by **arid climatic conditions**.
 
• Due to **low rainfall** (less than 200 mm annually) and high temperatures, the vegetation is limited to **low-growing plants, shrubs, and thorny bushes.**
 
• Plants found in the Thar Desert include **Cacti, Acacia, and Prosopis juliflora**, which are well-adapted to survive in dry conditions.
 
• These plants exhibit **xerophytic adaptations**, such as reduced leaves, thick cuticles, and deep root systems to conserve water.
 
• The region is dominated by **grasses** and hardy shrubs, providing limited grazing opportunities for livestock.
 
• The sparse vegetation helps reduce **soil erosion** caused by strong winds in the desert.
 
• These plants play an important role in maintaining the **ecological balance** of the desert and supporting the local fauna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alpine Meadows**__

 __
 
• **Alpine meadows** are found in mountainous regions with high altitudes, such as the **Himalayas** or the Alps.
 
• These areas are characterized by **cool temperatures**, moderate rainfall, and flora such as grasses, mosses, and flowering plants.
 
• Such vegetation is not suitable for the arid conditions of the Thar Desert.
 
 
 
• **Evergreen Forests**__
 __
 
• **Evergreen forests** are dense forests found in regions with high rainfall and moderate to warm temperatures, such as the **Western Ghats** or the northeastern states of India.
 
• These forests maintain their foliage throughout the year and are rich in biodiversity.
 
• The Thar Desert's climate does not support the growth of evergreen forests.
 
 
 
• **Stone Forests**__
 
 
• **Stone forests** refer to unique geological formations made of limestone or other sedimentary rocks, commonly seen in regions like **China's Stone Forest in Yunnan Province.**
 
• These are not vegetative landscapes and are unrelated to the vegetation types found in the Thar Desert.

questions.question: The distance between the easternmost and westernmost points of India is approximately:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**2933 km**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **distance between the easternmost and westernmost points of India** is approximately **2933 km**.
 
• The easternmost point of India is **Kibithu, Arunachal Pradesh**, located near the border with Myanmar and China.
 
• The westernmost point of India is **Guhar Moti, Gujarat**, located near the border with Pakistan in the Kutch region.
 
• The measurement of this distance reflects India’s **geographical expanse**, showcasing the country's vastness from east to west.
 
• India is the **7th largest country** in the world in terms of area, and its east-west stretch contributes significantly to its large geographical size.
 
• This distance is important for understanding **logistical planning, transport, and connectivity** across the nation.
 
• The geographical diversity between these points ranges from **mountainous terrains in the east** to **desert and coastal landscapes in the west**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Incorrect Options**__

 __
 
• While options such as **3500 km**, **2500 km**, and **3214 km** are close approximations, they do not accurately reflect the correct distance of **2933 km**.
 
• It is important to note that such figures are often rounded off, but precise measurements are crucial in geography-related questions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Geographical Knowledge**__
 
 
• Understanding the geographical dimensions of India helps in **planning infrastructure, transportation, and connectivity.**
 
• It also provides insights into the **diverse cultural and natural landscapes** that exist across the country.

questions.question: The Shivalik Hills, forming the outermost part of the Himalayan ranges, extend across which Indian states?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Jammu and Kashmir to Uttarakhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shivalik Hills**, also known as the Outer Himalayas, are the **southernmost range of the Himalayan mountain system**.
 
• The Shivalik range stretches from **Jammu and Kashmir** in the west to **Uttarakhand** in the east, covering parts of Himachal Pradesh as well.
 
• These hills are characterized by their **low altitude**, generally ranging between **600 to 1500 meters**.
 
• The range is known for its **narrow valleys** and **gravelly soil**, which is less stable compared to the higher Himalayan ranges.
 
• The Shivaliks act as a transitional zone between the **Gangetic plains** and the Himalayan ranges, providing a rich biodiversity and scenic beauty.
 
• Important rivers such as the **Ganga**, **Yamuna**, and **Beas** originate or flow through these regions.
 
• The region is home to several protected areas and national parks, such as **Rajaji National Park** in Uttarakhand.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh to Manipur**__

 __
 
• The region from **Arunachal Pradesh to Manipur** is part of the **Eastern Himalayas**, not the Shivalik Hills.
 
• This area is characterized by **dense forests** and is home to the **Patkai** and **Mikir Hills**.
 
• The Eastern Himalayas are known for their **high biodiversity** and are part of the Indo-Burma biodiversity hotspot.
 
 
 
• **Punjab to Sikkim**__
 __
 
• This stretch covers parts of the **Himalayan foothills**, but the Shivalik Hills are not continuous through this range.
 
• Sikkim is part of the **Eastern Himalayan range**, which is distinct from the Shivalik Hills.
 
• Punjab mainly features parts of the **northwestern Shivaliks**, but it doesn't extend all the way to Sikkim.
 
 
 
• **Bihar to West Bengal**__
 
 
• This region is part of the **Gangetic plains** and does not include the Shivalik Hills.
 
• The area is primarily known for its **alluvial soil** and agricultural productivity.
 
• Rivers like the **Ganga**, **Son**, and **Kosi** dominate this region.

questions.question: Which of the following brings winter rainfall to northern plains of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Western disturbances**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Western disturbances** are extratropical storms originating in the **Mediterranean region**.
 
• They travel eastward and bring **winter rainfall** to the **northern plains of India**, particularly in **Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• These disturbances are caused due to the westerly winds in the upper atmosphere, which carry moisture from the **Mediterranean Sea**, the **Atlantic Ocean**, and sometimes even from the **Caspian Sea**.
 
• The rainfall brought by these disturbances is crucial for the **rabi crops**, especially **wheat**, in northern India.
 
• They usually occur during the **winter months**, from December to February, though they can sometimes extend into early March.
 
• The interaction of Western disturbances with the Himalayas often leads to snowfall in the **higher altitudes** and rainfall in the plains.
 
• This phenomenon plays a significant role in maintaining the **climate balance** in the region by lowering temperatures and providing moisture.
 
• Western disturbances are also responsible for causing **cold waves** in northern India during winters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Norwesters**__

 __
 
• **Norwesters**, also called **Kalbaisakhi** in India, are thunderstorms that occur during the **pre-monsoon season**, mainly in **eastern India**, such as West Bengal, Assam, and Odisha.
 
• These storms are characterized by strong winds, heavy rainfall, and sometimes hailstorms, but they are not responsible for winter rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Bay of Bengal cyclones**__
 __
 
• **Bay of Bengal cyclones** are tropical cyclones that form over the **Bay of Bengal**, typically during the **pre-monsoon (April-May)** and **post-monsoon (October-November)** seasons.
 
• These cyclones are responsible for heavy rainfall in the eastern coastal states of India but do not impact the winter rainfall in northern plains.
 
 
 
• **Easterlies**__
 
 
• **Easterlies** are trade winds that blow from the east to the west in the **tropical regions**.
 
• They are associated with the monsoon season in India and do not contribute to winter rainfall in the northern plains.

questions.question: Which of the following lakes in Rajasthan is artificial?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Ana Sagar Lake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ana Sagar Lake** is an **artificial lake** located in Ajmer, Rajasthan.
 
• It was built in the **12th century** by **Arnoraja**, also known as **Ana**, who was the grandfather of Prithviraj Chauhan.
 
• The lake was constructed by building a dam across the **Luni River**.
 
• The lake covers an area of approximately **12 square kilometers** and is a popular tourist attraction in Ajmer.
 
• It is surrounded by beautiful gardens like **Daulat Bagh**, which were built by **Emperor Jahangir**.
 
• Ana Sagar Lake is an important example of **medieval engineering** and showcases the efforts to manage water resources in Rajasthan's arid climate.
 
• The lake also features a **Baradari (marble pavilion)** constructed during the Mughal period by Emperor Shah Jahan.
 
• The lake is a significant landmark and plays a vital role in the local ecosystem by supporting flora and fauna.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ramgarh Lake**__

 __
 
• Located near Jaipur, **Ramgarh Lake** is a natural water body surrounded by hills.
 
• It is a seasonal lake and often dries up during the summer months.
 
• The lake was once a major source of water for Jaipur and has historical significance.
 
 
 
• **Pushkar Lake**__
 __
 
• **Pushkar Lake** is a natural lake located in the town of Pushkar, Rajasthan.
 
• It is considered sacred and is surrounded by **52 bathing ghats** and numerous temples.
 
• The lake is a significant pilgrimage site for Hindus and is associated with the legend of Lord Brahma.
 
 
 
• **Sambhar Lake**__
 
 
• **Sambhar Lake** is India's largest inland saline lake, located near Jaipur.
 
• The lake is a natural formation and is known for its **salt production**.
 
• It is also a wetland of international importance under the **Ramsar Convention**.

questions.question: What is the major reason behind higher road density in Kerala compared to Rajasthan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Topography and population density**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kerala’s topography and population density** are key factors contributing to its higher road density compared to Rajasthan.
 
• Kerala has a **dense population of 859 persons per square kilometer** (Census 2011), requiring a robust road network for connectivity.
 
• The state’s **topography is dominated by undulating terrain and coastal plains**, which makes road construction more feasible than in Rajasthan's vast desert regions.
 
• Rajasthan, with a population density of **200 persons per square kilometer**, has vast arid and desert areas, making road construction challenging and less economically viable.
 
• Kerala’s high literacy rate and economic activities also demand better infrastructure, including roads, to support urbanization and trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Road density**: It is defined as the total length of roads per unit area or per unit population. Higher road density indicates better connectivity and infrastructure.
 
• **Topography**: The physical features of a region, such as plains, mountains, or deserts, significantly influence the feasibility and cost of road construction.
 
• **Population density**: Regions with higher population densities, like Kerala, require better connectivity to meet the transportation needs of the people.
 
• **Desert terrain in Rajasthan**: The Thar Desert covers a significant portion of Rajasthan, making road construction expensive and less practical in sparsely populated areas.
 
• **Economic factors**: Kerala’s economic activities, such as tourism, trade, and agriculture, necessitate a dense and well-maintained road network for accessibility and development.

questions.question: Indira Point, the southernmost tip of India, is located on which island?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Great Nicobar Island**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Indira Point is the southernmost tip of India, located on **Great Nicobar Island** in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
 
• It is situated at **6°45'10" N latitude** and **93°49'36" E longitude**, making it the southernmost geographical point of India.
 
• Indira Point was formerly known as **Pygmalion Point** before being renamed in honor of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• The location was significantly affected by the **2004 Indian Ocean tsunami**, which caused submersion of parts of the area.
 
• Great Nicobar Island is the largest island in the Nicobar group and is home to the **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve**, known for its rich biodiversity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nicobar Islands:**

 
 
• The Nicobar Islands are part of the Union Territory of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, located in the Indian Ocean.
 
• They consist of 22 islands divided into three groups: North Nicobar, Central Nicobar, and South Nicobar.
 
• The indigenous communities residing here include the **Nicotanese** and **Shompen tribes**.
 
 
 
• **2004 Indian Ocean Tsunami:**
 
 
• The tsunami was triggered by a massive earthquake off the coast of Sumatra, Indonesia, measuring **9.1-9.3 on the Richter scale**.
 
• It caused widespread destruction across coastal regions, including Indira Point, where the land submerged partially.
 
• Great Nicobar Island was one of the worst-hit areas, leading to loss of lives and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• It is a UNESCO-designated biosphere reserve, known for its unique flora and fauna.
 
• Species like **saltwater crocodiles, Nicobar megapodes, and leatherback turtles** are found here.
 
• Efforts are being undertaken to conserve the biodiversity of this region.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance:**
 
 
• Great Nicobar Island has strategic importance due to its proximity to the Strait of Malacca, a key maritime trade route.
 
• India is developing infrastructure projects like the **Nicobar Transshipment Port** to enhance its presence in the region.

questions.question: Which river system is known for forming gorges in the Himalayan region?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Brahmaputra River is renowned for forming deep gorges in the Himalayan region, especially in Arunachal Pradesh and Tibet.
 
• The Yarlung Tsangpo Grand Canyon, carved by the Brahmaputra in Tibet, is the world’s deepest gorge.
 
• In Arunachal Pradesh, the Brahmaputra flows through a gorge near the Namcha Barwa mountain, creating a dramatic landscape.
 
• These gorges are formed due to the river’s high velocity and the steep gradient of the Himalayas.
 
• The Brahmaputra is one of the major transboundary rivers, originating from the Angsi Glacier in Tibet and flowing through India and Bangladesh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gorge Formation:**

 
 
• A gorge is a deep valley with steep sides, often formed by rivers cutting through resistant rock layers.
 
• In the Himalayan region, rapid tectonic uplift combined with river erosion contributes to gorge formation.
 
 
 
• **Himalayan Rivers:**
 
 
• Himalayan rivers like the Indus, Ganga, and Brahmaputra are perennial, fed by glaciers and monsoon rains.
 
• These rivers often exhibit erosional features like gorges, waterfalls, and rapids.
 
 
 
• **Transboundary Rivers:**
 
 
• The Brahmaputra is a transboundary river, flowing through Tibet (China), India, and Bangladesh.
 
• It plays a crucial role in irrigation, hydropower, and biodiversity in its basin regions.
 
 
 
• **Yarlung Tsangpo River:**
 
 
• In Tibet, the Brahmaputra is known as the Yarlung Tsangpo.
 
• It originates near Mount Kailash and is an important river in the Tibetan Plateau.

questions.question: Which of the following states is NOT covered by the Ganga Plain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ganga Plain, also known as the Indo-Gangetic Plain, spans across several northern and eastern states of India, including Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal.
 
• Punjab is geographically located in the northwestern part of India and is primarily part of the Indus Basin, not the Ganga Basin.
 
• The Ganga Plain is characterized by fertile alluvial soil deposited by the Ganga River and its tributaries, supporting dense agriculture.
 
• Haryana, despite being geographically close to Punjab, has a small portion in the Yamuna-Ganga Plain region, making it partially included in the Ganga Plain.
 
• West Bengal and Bihar are major regions in the eastern Ganga Plain, receiving significant contributions from the Ganga and its tributaries.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Gangetic Plain:**

 
 
• It is one of the largest and most fertile plains in the world, covering northern and eastern India, parts of Pakistan, Nepal, and Bangladesh.
 
• It is primarily drained by the Ganga, Brahmaputra, and Indus river systems.
 
• The plain plays a critical role in India's agriculture, producing major crops like wheat, rice, sugarcane, and pulses.
 
 
 
• **Punjab Geography:**
 
 
• Punjab lies in the Indus Basin and is mainly drained by the Sutlej, Beas, and Ravi rivers.
 
• The state is known for its extensive canal irrigation system and is called the "Granary of India" due to its agricultural dominance.
 
 
 
• **Ganga River System:**
 
 
• The Ganga River originates from the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarakhand and flows through several states before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Major tributaries include Yamuna, Gandak, Kosi, and Son.
 
• The river basin supports over 500 million people, making it one of the most densely populated regions globally.
 
 
 
• **Haryana's Ganga Plain Connection:**
 
 
• Haryana is partially included in the Yamuna-Ganga Plain due to the Yamuna River flowing through the state.
 
• Its geographical connection to the Ganga Plain is limited but significant in terms of irrigation and agriculture.

questions.question: Which physiographic feature lies parallel to the Shiwaliks and is about 8-16 km wide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhabar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bhabar** is a narrow belt of 8-16 km in width lying parallel to the southern edge of the Shiwalik hills.
 
• This region is characterized by coarse alluvial deposits made up of pebbles and boulders brought down by the rivers descending from the Himalayas.
 
• It is marked by a high porosity of soil, causing streams and rivers to disappear and flow underground.
 
• The Bhabar zone is unsuitable for cultivation due to its rocky terrain and coarse soil texture.
 
• This belt serves as a transition zone between the hilly areas of the Shiwaliks and the fertile plains of the Terai region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shiwalik Hills:**

 
 
• Also known as the Outer Himalayas, the Shiwalik hills are the southernmost range of the Himalayas.
 
• They are composed of unconsolidated sediments, making them prone to erosion.
 
• The width of this range varies between 10 and 50 km, and its altitude ranges from 600 to 1500 meters.
 
 
 
• **Terai Region:**
 
 
• The Terai is a low-lying, marshy region lying south of the Bhabar belt.
 
• Unlike the Bhabar, the streams in this region re-emerge on the surface, making the area highly fertile and suitable for agriculture.
 
• The Terai is also home to rich biodiversity and dense forests, such as those found in Jim Corbett National Park.
 
 
 
• **Doab:**
 
 
• A doab refers to the fertile land between two converging rivers.
 
• For example, the Ganga-Yamuna Doab is one of the most agriculturally productive regions in India.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Deposits:**
 
 
• Alluvium is a loose soil or sediment deposited by rivers, typically consisting of sand, silt, and clay.
 
• Regions like the Indo-Gangetic plain owe their fertility to alluvial deposits brought by Himalayan rivers.

questions.question: The Thar Desert serves as a natural boundary between:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India and Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, serves as a natural geographical boundary between **India and Pakistan**.
 
• It is located primarily in the Indian state of Rajasthan, with smaller portions extending into Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana, as well as parts of Pakistan's Sindh province.
 
• The desert spans approximately **200,000 square kilometers**, making it the 17th largest desert in the world.
 
• The Thar Desert is characterized by its arid climate, vast sand dunes, and sparse vegetation, playing a crucial role in shaping the geography and culture of the region.
 
• The boundary formed by the Thar Desert has historically influenced cross-border trade, migration, and geopolitical relations between India and Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geographical Features of the Thar Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert consists of shifting sand dunes, rocky terrain, and saline lakes.
 
• It is primarily fed by the **monsoon rains**, receiving an annual rainfall of about 100-500 mm.
 
• Prominent rivers such as the **Luni River** flow through the desert region.
 
 
 
• **Climate and Biodiversity:**
 
 
• The Thar Desert experiences an **extreme climate**, with temperatures ranging from 0°C in winter to 50°C in summer.
 
• The desert is home to unique flora and fauna, including species like the Indian gazelle (Chinkara), desert fox, and various reptiles.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Cultural Importance:**
 
 
• The desert supports agriculture and animal husbandry, particularly camel rearing, which is vital for transportation and livelihood.
 
• It is rich in minerals such as gypsum, bentonite, and limestone, contributing to India's mining sector.
 
• Cultural festivals like the **Desert Festival of Jaisalmer** attract tourists and celebrate the heritage of the region.
 
 
 
• **Border Relations:**
 
 
• The Thar Desert serves as a **natural barrier** in the India-Pakistan border region, limiting military movement in certain areas.
 
• Several border posts and fences have been established along the desert to enhance security and monitor cross-border activities.

questions.question: Which of the following is the easternmost international border point of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kibithu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kibithu** is located in the Anjaw district of Arunachal Pradesh, India, and is the easternmost inhabited village near the international border with China.
 
• It is strategically significant as it lies at the tri-junction of India, China, and Myanmar, making it vital for border security and trade.
 
• Kibithu is situated at an altitude of approximately 4,070 feet above sea level, offering stunning views of the Lohit River valley.
 
• This area was a crucial point of engagement during the 1962 Sino-Indian War, and it continues to be a region of strategic importance for India’s defense forces.
 
• Due to its geographical location, Kibithu plays a critical role in monitoring and maintaining the integrity of India’s eastern borders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nathu La:**

 
 
• Located in Sikkim, Nathu La is a mountain pass on the Indo-China border, crucial for trade and military operations.
 
• It connects India’s Sikkim state with China’s Tibet Autonomous Region.
 
 
 
• **Lipulekh:**
 
 
• Located in Uttarakhand, Lipulekh Pass serves as a gateway to Kailash Mansarovar in Tibet.
 
• The pass is part of the disputed Kalapani region claimed by both India and Nepal.
 
 
 
• **Rohtang:**
 
 
• Rohtang Pass is situated in Himachal Pradesh, connecting Kullu Valley with Lahaul and Spiti Valley.
 
• It is not located near India’s international borders.
 
 
 
• **India's Easternmost Point:**
 
 
• The easternmost point of India is not Kibithu but the disputed territory of Vijaynagar in Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• Kibithu is the easternmost international border settlement in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is a tributary of the Yamuna river?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Tons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Tons River** is one of the largest and most important **tributaries** of the Yamuna River.
 
• It originates from the **Bandarpunch Glacier** in the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand.
 
• The Tons River merges with the Yamuna near **Kalsi** in the Dehradun district of Uttarakhand.
 
• The river is known for its **rugged terrain and steep gorges**, making it a significant river in the Himalayan region.
 
• The Tons River is also popular for **adventure sports** like rafting due to its high-speed water currents.
 
• This river contributes significantly to the **water flow** of the Yamuna, especially during the monsoon season.
 
• It flows through regions rich in **biodiversity** and passes through dense forests and valleys.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Son River**__

 __
 
• The Son River is a **major tributary of the Ganga**, not the Yamuna.
 
• It originates from **Amarkantak Plateau** in Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It flows through states like **Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand, and Bihar**.
 
• The river is known for its sandy riverbed and **seasonal flow variations**.
 
 
 
• **Teesta River**__
 __
 
• The Teesta River is a **tributary of the Brahmaputra**, not the Yamuna.
 
• It originates from the **Tso Lhamo Lake** in North Sikkim.
 
• The river flows through **Sikkim and West Bengal**, and then enters Bangladesh.
 
• It is a vital source of **irrigation and hydroelectricity** in the region.
 
 
 
• **Gomti River**__
 
 
• The Gomti River is a **tributary of the Ganga**, not the Yamuna.
 
• It originates from **Gomat Taal** (also known as Fulhar Lake) near Madhotanda in Uttar Pradesh.
 
• The river flows entirely within **Uttar Pradesh** and passes through cities like Lucknow.
 
• The Gomti is considered sacred in Hindu tradition and is linked to **religious practices**.

questions.question: The Shillong Plateau is divided into several parts. Which of the following is not a part of it?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Maikala Range**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shillong Plateau** is a significant geographical feature located in the northeastern part of India.
 
• It is primarily divided into three distinct regions: the **Khasi Hills**, **Jaintia Hills**, and **Garo Hills**.

questions.question: What is the typical direction of jet streams influencing the Indian climate in winter?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**West to east**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In winter, the **jet streams** influencing the Indian climate typically flow from **west to east**.
 
• Jet streams are fast-moving air currents found in the upper levels of the atmosphere, mainly in the **troposphere**.
 
• These streams play a vital role in shaping the **weather patterns**, especially during winter months.
 
• The western jet stream influences the Indian subcontinent, bringing **cold weather conditions** and impacting the western disturbances.
 
• The western disturbances, driven by these jet streams, are responsible for the **winter rainfall** in the northwestern parts of India.
 
• The direction of jet streams is primarily governed by the **rotation of the Earth** and the temperature contrast between the equator and poles.
 
• During winter, the position of the jet streams shifts southward, influencing the weather over **South Asia**, including India.
 
• The west-to-east flow of jet streams also impacts the movement of cyclonic systems in the region, contributing to the formation of **rain-bearing clouds**.
 
• These jet streams have a significant effect on agriculture, as winter rainfall supports the **Rabi crop season**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **East to west**__

 __
 
• Jet streams typically do not flow from **east to west** due to the Earth's rotation and the temperature gradient between the poles and the equator.
 
• This direction would contradict the general movement of atmospheric circulation in the Northern Hemisphere.
 
 
 
• **Southwest to northeast**__
 __
 
• This direction is commonly associated with the movement of the **Southwest Monsoon winds** in India during the summer season, not winter.
 
• The monsoon winds are influenced by the heating of the Indian Ocean and the Himalayas, which is distinct from the jet streams.
 
 
 
• **Southeast to northwest**__
 
 
• Jet streams in this direction are unusual and do not align with the typical atmospheric circulation observed in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• This option is not relevant for the Indian winter climate influenced by jet streams.
